class.name: NetwDisplayTiming
class.brief_description: One pump's timing snapshot, the plain scalars a display runtime reads instead of a clock.
class.description: A display runtime never resolves or reads a clock. The pump captures one snapshot at the top of the frame and hands the same one to every runtime, so a runtime's sample math depends only on scalars owned by that frame and a pump over one entity touches nothing outside that entity. That is what makes a runtime pump orderable and, later, parallelisable. [codeblock] var timing = NetwDisplayTiming.capture(clock, frame_delta) for runtime in book.runtimes(): pump_runtime(runtime, timing) # timing crosses by value, never a clock [/codeblock] Every field is writable, because a test rig declares a timeline directly rather than standing a clock up to produce one.

method.name: capture
method.description: Reads one snapshot from [param clock], pairing it with the wall-clock [param frame_delta] since the previous pump. A null [param clock] yields a zeroed snapshot rather than a refusal, so a pump that runs before any configurator has registered a clock stays inert instead of failing.

members.member: Ticks the display clock trails the simulation, which is the buffer depth that guarantees a later snapshot to interpolate toward.
The display clock tick, already trailing [member tick] by [member display_offset].
Wall-clock seconds since the previous pump. This is the display smoothing delta, and it is the one field in the snapshot that is not tick-space.
Ticks elapsed in this frame, [member frame_delta] times the clock's tickrate.
The [member display_offset] the clock recommends given the jitter it has measured. A playhead dilates toward this rather than snapping to it.
Fractional progress from [member display_tick] toward the next tick.
